HISTORY: Recently diagnosed left breast moderately differentiated invasive ductal  carcinoma with positive left axillary nodal metastasis. COMPARISON: Comparison has been made to previous images.  TECHNIQUE: MR BREAST W AND WO IV CONTRAST BILATERAL was performed on a 1.5 tesla  magnet utilizing axial T1, axial T2 weighted images, axial fat suppressed  gradient echo T1 weighted pulse sequences were obtained. Pre-gadolinium,  arterial, and interstitial phases of enhancement were obtained  sequentially. Delayed sagittal T1 weighted images were obtained.  Subtraction images were generated by post processing.  Contrast administered: gadobenate dimeglumine (MULTIHANCE) 529 MG/ML  injection 9 mL, Total Given: 9 mL (1 dose) intravenously without  significant complications.  FINDINGS: The breast has scattered fibroglandular tissue. The background parenchymal enhancement is mild and symmetric.   Left In the lower outer quadrant, there is an enhancing bilobed mass measuring  14 x 18 mm in axial dimension, best seen at slice location -40.8.  There  is an associated biopsy clip artifact.  There are two additional enhancing masses in the deep upper central breast  that are adjacent to each other.  The more superior mass measures 6 mm  (slice location 54.2) and the more inferior mass measures 8 mm (slice  location 42.2).  There is a heterogeneous lobulated collection in the left axilla with mild  rim enhancement, most likely represent post-biopsy changes and hematoma  secondary to core biopsy.  Right No suspicious enhancing lesions are seen.
